chunks.title: Abbey Views: summary card
chunks.text: Abbey Views. Best for couples. Location: Bath city centre. Rating 4.91 (218). A stylish apartment for two with views of the 18th-century Abbey, two minutes from the Roman Baths and Thermae Spa. 2 guests, 1 bedroom, 1 bathroom.

chunks.title: Longscroft Manor: summary card
chunks.text: Longscroft Manor. Best for groups & families. Location: Near Bradford-on-Avon, Wiltshire. Rating 4.81 (63). A five-bedroom manor a short drive from Bath, with large gardens, a BBQ, a fire pit and free parking on site. 12 guests, 5 bedrooms, 2.5 bathrooms.

chunks.title: Things to do: Bath Abbey
chunks.text: Bath Abbey. 1 min walk from Abbey Views. The view from your window, up close. Admire the fan-vaulted ceiling and the famous "Jacob's ladder" west front. Category: history.

chunks.title: Things to do: The Pump Room
chunks.text: The Pump Room. 1 min walk from Abbey Views. Georgian elegance for afternoon tea or brunch, with live music and a taste of the spa waters. Category: food history.

chunks.title: Things to do: The Roman Baths
chunks.text: The Roman Baths. 2 min walk from Abbey Views. The best-preserved Roman spa in northern Europe, with the sacred spring still flowing. The city's must-see. Category: history.

chunks.title: Things to do: Thermae Bath Spa
chunks.text: Thermae Bath Spa. 2 min walk from Abbey Views. Soak in naturally warm mineral water, with a rooftop pool that looks out across the city. Category: spa.

chunks.title: Things to do: Sally Lunn's
chunks.text: Sally Lunn's. 3 min walk from Abbey Views. Bath's famous historic eating house, home of the Sally Lunn bun, in one of the city's oldest houses. Category: food.

chunks.title: Things to do: Theatre Royal Bath
chunks.text: Theatre Royal Bath. 4 min walk from Abbey Views. A beautiful Georgian theatre staging West End tours, plays and pantomime year-round. Category: history.

chunks.title: Things to do: Parade Gardens & the River Avon
chunks.text: Parade Gardens & the River Avon. 5 min walk from Abbey Views. A riverside garden right by Pulteney Bridge. Perfect for a picnic, a deckchair and the weir views. Category: outdoors.

chunks.title: Things to do: Pulteney Bridge
chunks.text: Pulteney Bridge. 6 min walk from Abbey Views. One of the few bridges in the world lined with shops on both sides. Best photographed from the weir. Category: history outdoors.

chunks.title: Things to do: Jane Austen Centre
chunks.text: Jane Austen Centre. 10 min walk from Abbey Views. Step into Regency Bath and the author's time in the city. Look out for costumed guides on Gay Street. Category: history.

chunks.title: Things to do: Green Park Station Market
chunks.text: Green Park Station Market. 10 min walk from Abbey Views. Local producers, street food and independent stalls under a restored Victorian station roof, at weekends. Category: food.

chunks.title: Things to do: The Royal Crescent & The Circus
chunks.text: The Royal Crescent & The Circus. approx. 15 min walk from Abbey Views. Thirty sweeping Georgian townhouses around a lawn that rolls down to Royal Victoria Park. Go early and you might spot the hot-air balloons. Category: history outdoors.

chunks.title: Things to do: Prior Park Landscape Garden
chunks.text: Prior Park Landscape Garden. Short bus or taxi ride from Abbey Views. A Palladian garden with a picture-perfect view over the city, and the start of the Bath Skyline countryside trail. Category: outdoors.

chunks.title: Things to do: Bradford-on-Avon
chunks.text: Bradford-on-Avon. Near Longscroft Manor (a short drive). A honey-stone town on the River Avon, with a medieval Tithe Barn, a tiny Saxon church and riverside pubs. Category: near the manor history.

chunks.title: Things to do: Kennet & Avon Canal
chunks.text: Kennet & Avon Canal. Near Longscroft Manor (a short drive). Flat towpath walks and bike rides past narrowboats to the Avoncliff Aqueduct, with canal-side cafés along the way. Category: near the manor outdoors.

chunks.title: Things to do: Iford Manor Gardens
chunks.text: Iford Manor Gardens. Near Longscroft Manor (a short drive). Harold Peto's Italianate terraced garden in a quiet river valley. Opening is seasonal, so check before you go. Category: near the manor outdoors.

chunks.title: Things to do: Lacock
chunks.text: Lacock. Near Longscroft Manor (a short drive). A National Trust village and abbey, familiar from film and TV, with a museum dedicated to the birth of photography. Category: near the manor history.

chunks.title: FAQ (Both stays): What time are check-in and check-out?
chunks.text: What time are check-in and check-out? Check-in is after 16:00 and check-out is before 10:00 at both properties.

chunks.title: FAQ (Both stays): How do I book and pay?
chunks.text: How do I book and pay? Choose a stay and your dates in the booking form to see the full price, including our direct-booking discount. Then add your details and pay securely by card, Apple Pay or Google Pay. Payments are handled by Stripe, and you're only charged once your dates are confirmed.

chunks.title: FAQ (Both stays): How does check-in work?
chunks.text: How does check-in work? Both stays have self check-in, so you can arrive at your own pace. Abbey Views uses a lockbox and Longscroft Manor a key safe on site. We send full instructions before you travel.

chunks.title: FAQ (Both stays): Who looks after the properties?
chunks.text: Who looks after the properties? Both properties are managed by AIR Development Consultancy Ltd. Get in touch before or during your stay and we'll be happy to help.

chunks.title: FAQ (Abbey Views): Are there stairs?
chunks.text: Are there stairs? The apartment is on the fourth floor. A lift takes you to the third floor, followed by around 15 stairs to the front door. Please bear this in mind if you have mobility needs or heavy luggage.

chunks.title: FAQ (Abbey Views): Where can I park?
chunks.text: Where can I park? The nearest recommended car parks are Southgate and Manvers Street, both about a 5-minute walk away.

chunks.title: FAQ (Abbey Views): Can we check in early or leave late?
chunks.text: Can we check in early or leave late? Early check-in and late check-out may be available on request. Charges apply.

chunks.title: FAQ (Longscroft Manor): Is there parking?
chunks.text: Is there parking? Yes, there is ample free parking on site.

chunks.title: FAQ (Longscroft Manor): Can we bring our dog?
chunks.text: Can we bring our dog? Sorry, dogs are not accepted at Longscroft Manor.

chunks.title: FAQ (Longscroft Manor): Is it suitable for young children?
chunks.text: Is it suitable for young children? Yes. A travel cot and high chair are available on request, and the bunk room is a favourite with kids.

chunks.title: How to book and check availability
chunks.text: To check dates and book, use the "Plan your stay" form at the top of any page: choose a property, check-in and check-out dates and the number of guests. The calendar only lets you pick dates that are free, and the total price appears once both dates are chosen. Then press the button to continue to the secure checkout, where you add your details and pay by card, Apple Pay or Google Pay. Abbey Views sleeps up to 2. Longscroft Manor sleeps up to 12.

chunks.title: Longscroft Manor: overview
chunks.text: Country manor · Wiltshire. 4.81 · 63 reviews · Sleeps 12. 4.81 · 63 reviews, Near Bradford-on-Avon, Sleeps 12. A handsome five-bedroom manor on the outskirts of Bradford-on-Avon, a short drive from Bath. Two spacious reception rooms, a farmhouse-style kitchen, a dining table for the whole group, and large gardens with a BBQ, outdoor seating and a fire pit. Ideal for family gatherings, reunions and celebration weekends. Highlights: Sleeps 12 across 5 bedrooms: Plus a travel cot and high chair on request. Large gardens: BBQ, outdoor seating and a fire pit for long evenings. Free parking on site: Plenty of space for several cars.
